info.name: CRM Sales Management API
info.description:
REST API for a CRM sales process: Lead -> Customer -> Deal, with activities, timeline and analytics.

**How to use**
1. Run the server (`npm run dev`) and seed demo data (`npm run seed -- --fresh`).
2. Send **Auth / Login (Admin)**. Its test script stores `accessToken` in the collection variables.
3. Every other request uses Bearer `{{accessToken}}` (set on the collection).
4. "Create" requests store the new IDs (`leadId`, `customerId`, `dealId`, ...) automatically, so the folders can be run top to bottom (or with the Collection Runner).

**Response format**
Success: `{ "success": true, "message": "...", "data": {...}, "meta": {...pagination} }`
Error: `{ "success": false, "message": "...", "errors": [{ "field", "message" }] }`

**Roles**: `admin`, `sales_manager`, `sales_executive`. Records outside a user's scope return 404.

request.description: Public. Returns 200 when the API is running.

item.name: Users (Admin)
item.description: User management. All endpoints are admin-only except `GET /users/team` (admin + manager).

request.description: Admin only. Roles: `admin`, `sales_manager`, `sales_executive`.

query.description: name, email, role, createdAt... prefix - for desc

Admin only. 400 invalid ID, 404 not found.
Admin only. Any of name, email, phone, password, role, manager. Cannot change own role. A manager with team members cannot be demoted.

item.name: Leads
item.description: Lead management, assignment, status workflow, conversion and timeline. Executives only see leads assigned to them; managers see their team's leads.

request.description:
All roles. Executives are auto-assigned to themselves. Admin/manager may set `assignedTo` (active executive; manager: own team only).

source: Website | Referral | Social Media | Email | Phone | Other
priority: Low | Medium | High
Either email or phone is required. 409 if an active lead with the same email exists.
All roles (scoped).
Includes convertedCustomer / convertedDeal once converted.
Fields: name, email, phone, company, source, priority, description. Priority changes are recorded as `lead_priority_changed`. Converted leads are read-only (409).

Allowed transitions:
New -> Contacted, Qualified, Unqualified, Lost
Contacted -> Qualified, Unqualified, Lost
Qualified -> Contacted, Unqualified, Lost
Unqualified -> Contacted, Lost
Lost -> Contacted
"Converted" is only set by the convert endpoint. Lost requires `reason`.
Lead must be Qualified before conversion.
Negative example: returns 400 because `reason` is missing.

Admin + manager. Assignee must be an active sales executive (manager: own team). Logged as `lead_assigned` / `lead_reassigned`.

(This example returns 400 "already assigned" because Create lead already assigned the same executive.)

Runs in a MongoDB transaction: creates the Customer (references the lead) and optional Deal (references customer and lead), marks the lead Converted and writes timeline entries. All or nothing.

Errors: 400 lead not Qualified / not assigned / invalid deal, 409 already converted.
Negative example: 409 "Lead has already been converted".
Audit history, newest first.
Admin + manager. Converted leads cannot be deleted (409), as in this example. Non-converted leads are deleted and the timeline entries are kept.

item.name: Customers
item.description: Customer management. Customers keep a reference to their original lead and expose their deals.

request.description: Executives are auto-assigned. Admin/manager must provide `assignedTo`. 409 duplicate email.
All roles (scoped).
Populates the original `lead` and the `deals` array.
Fields: name, email, phone, company, address, status, assignedTo (admin/manager only). Logged as `customer_updated` with before/after values.
Audit history of the customer.
Admin + manager. Blocked (409) when the customer has deals or was converted from a lead. Set status Inactive instead.

item.name: Deals
item.description: Deal management and stage workflow. Expected revenue = value x probability / 100, always computed by the server.

request.description: Customer must be accessible and Active. value > 0, probability 0-100 (default by stage), expectedCloseDate not in the past and within 5 years. Only active stages allowed on create.
All roles (scoped).
Populates customer, lead, assignedTo, createdBy.
Fields: name, value, probability, expectedCloseDate, description. Revenue is recalculated. Closed (Won/Lost) deals cannot be edited (409).
Probability resets to the stage default (Qualification 10, Discovery 25, Proposal 50, Negotiation 75) unless `probability` is sent.
Negative example: `lostReason` is required.
Requires an Active customer and value > 0. Sets probability 100, status Won and closedAt. Logged as `deal_stage_changed` + `deal_won`.
Closed deals cannot freely move back. Managers/executives get 409; admin gets 400 unless a `reason` is provided, e.g. `{ "stage": "Negotiation", "reason": "Client reopened talks" }`.

Admin + manager. Only open deals; assignee must be an active executive (manager: own team). Logged as `deal_assigned`.

(This example returns 400 "already assigned" because the converted deal inherited the same executive.)
Audit history of the deal.
Admin + manager. Won deals are revenue history and cannot be deleted (409), as in this example.

item.name: Activities
item.description: Calls, emails, meetings, demos, follow-ups, reminders and notes. Stored status is Pending/Completed; "Overdue" is computed by the backend (Pending + dueDate in the past).

request.description:
type: Call | Email | Meeting | Demo | Follow-up | Reminder | Note
relatedType: Lead | Customer | Deal | User (must be accessible)
dueDate is required (except Note) and cannot be in the past. Executives can only create activities for themselves.
Notes are saved as Completed and logged as `note_added` on the deal timeline.
Default sort: soonest due first.
Fields: title, description, dueDate, assignedTo. Completed activities are read-only (409).
Sets status Completed + completedAt. Logged as `follow_up_completed` / `activity_completed`. Completing twice returns 409.
Admin/manager: any accessible activity. Executive: only pending activities they created.

item.name: Dashboard
item.description: Sales analytics built with aggregation pipelines. All endpoints are role-scoped and accept optional `from` / `to` (createdAt range).

request.description: Total/new/qualified/converted leads, customers, open/won/lost deals, total revenue (won), expected revenue (open, weighted), conversion rate, win rate, pending/overdue activities.
Number of deals, total value, expected revenue and average probability for every stage, in pipeline order.
Admin + manager (403 for executives). Per executive: leads, conversion rate, deals won/lost, win rate, revenue won, open pipeline, pending/overdue activities. Sorted by revenue.
